t: Galvanic Isolation: Breaking the Copper Path
title: Galvanic Isolation: Breaking the Copper Path
description: Galvanic isolation breaks the direct electrical connection between two circuits while letting signals cross — no shared ground, no current path for surges. Transformers, capacitors, and light do the crossing. Isolation is what keeps a high-voltage fault on one side from becoming a disaster on the other.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Optocouplers: Signals on Light
description: An optocoupler pairs an LED with a photodetector in one package: current through the LED becomes light, light becomes current on the other side, with kilovolts of isolation between. The classic 4N25-style part has isolated thousands of industrial interfaces. Light crosses; voltage does not.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Current Transfer Ratio (CTR)
description: CTR — output current over input current, in percent — is the optocoupler's gain: it varies with temperature, LED aging, and drive current, so designs derate it generously. A CTR of 50-600% is typical for transistor-output parts. Designing to worst-case CTR is the difference between working and flaky.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Digital Isolators: The Modern Replacement
description: Digital isolators (Analog Devices iCoupler, TI ISO77xx) replace LED optocouplers with on-chip transformers or capacitors: faster (150 Mbps), lower power, tighter timing, and longer life — no LED to age. They dominate new isolated digital designs. The optocoupler remains where proven simplicity wins.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Isolation Voltage Ratings
description: Isolation is rated in volts RMS or DC the barrier withstands — 2.5 kV, 5 kV, more — tested per UL 1577, IEC 60747-5-5, or VDE. Ratings assume creepage and clearance distances on the board, not just the package. The rating is only as good as the layout around it.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Common-Mode Transient Immunity (CMTI)
description: CMTI measures how fast a common-mode voltage spike the isolator tolerates without corrupting data — 100+ kV/µs for modern parts switching SiC/GaN gates. Motor drives and fast switchers live or die on CMTI. A slow isolator in a fast drive is a glitch generator.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Isolated Gate Drivers
description: Isolated gate drivers combine isolation with the muscle to switch power transistors — driving IGBT/SiC gates across the barrier with desaturation protection and Miller clamping. They are the standard interface between control logic and power stages. One package: isolation plus drive.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Reinforced vs Basic Isolation
description: Safety standards distinguish basic isolation (one barrier, needs a second protective measure) from reinforced (a single barrier rated as two). Medical and mains-connected equipment often requires reinforced. The distinction is in the standard's testing, not just the datasheet claim.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Side-Channel Defense by Isolation
description: Galvanic isolation also breaks side-channel paths: power-analysis and EM probes on one side see nothing of the cryptographic operations on the other. Secure hardware isolates its crypto island physically, not just logically. Defense in depth starts at the circuit level.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Analog Isolation: Linear Optocouplers
description: Linear optocouplers (HCNR201-style) pass analog signals across the barrier with a feedback photodiode servoing the LED — 0.01% linearity for isolated measurement. Current loops and medical sensing use them. Analog across isolation is harder than digital; the servo makes it honest.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Creepage and Clearance Layout
description: Creepage (along surfaces) and clearance (through air) distances on the PCB complete the isolation the package starts — standards tables set millimeters per voltage and pollution degree. Slots and moats in the board enforce it. The best isolator fails in a sloppy layout.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

t: Surge and ESD Across the Barrier
title: Surge and ESD Across the Barrier
description: Isolation barriers are surge-tested — kilovolt transients per IEC 61000-4-5 — to prove the barrier holds when the real world strikes. ESD guns test the human-touch case. Ratings on paper become ratings in the lab.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Choosing the Isolator
description: Isolator selection weighs speed, voltage, CMTI, power, channels, and lifetime against cost: digital isolators for fast data, optocouplers for proven analog and high-voltage niches, reinforced grades where safety demands. The application picks; the datasheet confirms.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Isolation for Cryptographic Hardware
description: Secure modules isolate key operations behind barriers — power, signal, and physical — so attacks must cross engineered boundaries. Isolation is one layer of the tamper-resistance stack alongside enclosures and sensors. Boundaries compound.
